title: Visitation Rights for Residents in Nursing Homes After 1 June
what_it_is: Visitation Rights for Residents in Nursing Homes After 1 June

sections.label: Eldercare activities and testing resumption
sections.summary: Phase One gradually resumes individual on-site activities at Senior Activity Centres, keeps nursing home visits suspended, and progressively tests eldercare staff.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In Phase One, on-site activities that can be done individually, like craftwork, reading and gardening, will gradually resume at Senior Activity Centres, with restrictions on the activity duration and the total number of persons per session.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Given that nursing home residents are generally more frail, face-to-face visits will continue to be suspended to keep the risk of infection low.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Nursing homes can also allow face-to-face visits in exceptional circumstances, such as when the patient is critically ill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We will progressively resume more activities across different settings when the situation improves.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We conduct surveillance testing for the eldercare sector, to complement existing precautionary measures such as safe distancing, visitor restrictions and infection control.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We prioritised swab tests for staff and clients at residential care homes in May and in June, we will progressively test staff of other eldercare services in operation, including those working at day-care centres.
